question: Who was the most prominent non-Congress leader among the members who contested the elections of the "Constituent Assembly" and was later made the Law Minister?
solution: Nehru and Patel rose above party politics and included the best talents in the assembly for the building of the country.

question: “Constituent Assembly” was a conspiracy hatched by the British – What was Somnath Lahiri's main argument behind this statement?
options: Continuation of the veto power of the Viceroy
solution: This idea of ​​Lahiri later proved to be wrong because the Indian leaders made the Assembly completely sovereign.

question: Who was appointed as the "Defence Minister" in the interim government?
solution: The Defense Ministry was a sensitive department which was given to Congress ally and Sikh leader Baldev Singh.

question: Who was the chief calligrapher of the "English" copy of the Indian Constitution?
solution: Prem Bihari Narayan Raizada did not take any money from the British Government in return, only sought permission to write his name on every page and his grandfather's name on the last page.

question: How many total seats were left in the Constituent Assembly after the boycott of "Muslim League"?
solution: Of these 299 members, only 284 ultimately signed the Constitution.

question: How much total budget was spent in making the Indian Constitution?
solution: This budget included expenses for the study of constitutions of various countries, meetings of committees and the secretariat.

question: What was the period for which the Constituent Assembly functioned as the "Provisional Parliament"?
solution: The first Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha of India were formed after the general elections of 1952.

question: Usha Nath Sen, the head of the committee formed to take the proceedings of the Constituent Assembly to the "Press Gallery", was associated with which profession?
solution: It was only due to the activeness of the Press Gallery Committee that the news of the making of the Constitution could be published in detail in the newspapers of that time.

question: Who was the Chairman of "Tribal and Excluded Areas Sub-committee"?
solution: Thakkar Bapa had dedicated his entire life to the welfare of tribal and backward castes.
